Fit the space-time areal model

Source: R/fit.R
fit_areal.Rd

Fits the model to the observed area-time cells of data by MCMC. The logit prevalence of cell (area \(a\), time \(t\)) is $$x_{at} = z_{at}^\top \beta + f_{at} + \epsilon_{at},$$ where \(z_{at}\) holds the fixed effects set by formula (by default an intercept and a linear trend in time), \(f\) is a Gaussian field with separable covariance (a Leroux prior on the frame's graph in space, with scale sigma and dependence rho_s; a unit-variance AR1 with correlation rho_t in time), and \(\epsilon\) is a cell-level nugget with standard deviation sigma_n. Positives are binomial given \(x\).

Usage

fit_areal(
  data,
  formula = ~trend(),
  covariates = NULL,
  scale_covariates = TRUE,
  nugget = TRUE,
  priors = areal_priors(),
  control = mcmc_control(),
  checkpoint_dir = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A areal_data() object (or a simulation from simulate_areal()).

formula

A one-sided formula for the fixed effects. It always has an intercept; trend() adds a linear trend in time (from -1 at the first time step to 1 at the last); other terms are names of columns of covariates. Factor or character covariates get one dummy per level after the first. Transforms and interactions must be made as columns.

covariates

A data frame, or a list of data frames, of covariates. Each is keyed by an id column (areas, for covariates that do not change over time), a t (step number) or time (label) column (for covariates the same in every area), or both (covariates by area and time). Each must cover every area, time step or area-time cell it is keyed by, since predictions are made everywhere.

scale_covariates

Standardise numeric covariates to mean 0 and sd 1, over the areas, time steps or cells they are given for, so that the default prior on their effects (sd 3, see areal_priors()) is weakly informative whatever their units. Effects are then per sd of the covariate; the centres and scales are in fit$design and in summary(). Unscaled covariates in large units (e.g. population counts) can make the prior variance of the mean so large that the field is lost in rounding; the fit then stops and says so.

nugget

Include the cell-level nugget.

priors

areal_priors(), or a list of some of its arguments.

control

mcmc_control(), or a list of some of its arguments.

checkpoint_dir

A folder to save each chain's state in. If a fit is interrupted, running it again with the same folder resumes every chain where it stopped, and gives exactly the draws of an uninterrupted run; a finished fit run again is read back from the folder. A folder left by a different fit (other data, frame, model or sampler settings) is refused. Use a folder outside synced storage (Dropbox, OneDrive), which can lock files. NULL: no checkpoints.

Value

An object of class stareal_fit:

trace

the hyperparameter trace, burn-in included: chain, iteration, the hyperparameters on the unconstrained scale (log_sigma, logit_rho_s, logit_rho_t, log_sigma_n), lp (the log prior of the hyperparameters plus the log density of the latent values given them; lp + ll is the unnormalised log joint), the log-likelihood ll, and the acceptance rates of the two hyperparameter moves

draws

the stored posterior draws, as arrays (draw x chain x variable): theta (unconstrained), beta, and x (logit prevalence of each observed cell, nugget included, in the order of data$cells)

stored_iter, seconds

the iterations the draws were stored at; run time per chain

design

the fixed-effect design: formula, names, and the centre and scale of each standardised covariate

data, priors, control, nugget, checkpoint_dir, call

as given (priors with one prior per fixed effect)

Use summary(), diagnose(), plot(), predict() and posterior::as_draws_df(fit) (or as_draws_array(), ...).

Details

The unobserved cells and the fixed effects are integrated out exactly, so the sampler works on the observed cells only; its cost per iteration grows as the cube of the number of observed cells. The full area-time surface is reconstructed afterwards by predict().

Examples

fr <- areal_lattice(4, 4)
tf <- time_frame(n_steps = 5)
sim <- simulate_areal(fr, tf, n_cells = 30, seed = 1)
fit <- fit_areal(sim, control = list(n_iter = 100, n_burn = 50, n_store = 25, n_chains = 1,
                                     ess_sweeps = 2, verbose = FALSE))
fit
#> <stareal_fit> 30 observed cells on 16 units x 5 time steps, with nugget
#>   formula ~trend(): intercept, trend
#>   1 chain x 100 iterations (50 burn-in); 25 stored draws in all; 0.078 s per chain
#>   posterior medians: sigma 1.33, rho_s 0.603, rho_t 0.905, sigma_n 0.252
#>   see summary(), diagnose(), plot() and predict()
